rationale: All three pins produce numerically identical output on the real issue-121 runtime, so the choice turns entirely on malformed and dropped-roster history, and codex is the only pin with no wrong-output defect that also reports a legacy run against the roster that actually ran: cursor's journal reader skips a malformed known event and reported 12527.62 min elapsed and 'in-progress' for a fixture run that completed in 45.00 min, while my own pin and cursor's both print a wait row for a dropped agent and would permanently block the cross-roster total on any legacy issue that dropped one; codex's remaining gaps (its cursors.json completion gate and its bundled tests) are smaller and additive to fix than either.
